partners.mechanism_chain: MANBA (HGNC:6884) —DISRUPTS→ Accumulation of incompletely degraded oligosaccharides (CHEBI:27348); Accumulation of incompletely degraded oligosaccharides (CHEBI:27348) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosomal storage (HP:0001361); NCKAP1L (HGNC:29341) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005767); Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005767) —LEADS_TO→ Immune dysregulation (HP:0002710); Lysosomal storage (HP:0001361) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal degradation pathway (GO:0005767). Loss-of-function mutations in MANBA lead to the accumulation of incompletely degraded oligosaccharides, causing lysosomal storage and subsequent cellular dysfunction characteristic of beta-mannosidosis. Concurrently, loss-of-function variants in NCKAP1L disrupt the broader lysosomal degradation pathway, contributing to immune dysregulation and autoinflammation in immunodeficiency 72. The convergence occurs as the lysosomal storage phenotype from MANBA dysfunction directly impacts the integrity and function of the shared lysosomal degradation pathway, exacerbating the cellular defects and potentially contributing to immune phenotypes.

partners.mechanism_chain: MANBA (HGNC:6890) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal hydrolysis of oligosaccharides (GO:0005708); Lysosomal hydrolysis of oligosaccharides (GO:0005708) —LEADS_TO→ Oligosaccharidosis (HP:0001031); HBA2 (HGNC:4834) —DISRUPTS→ Misfolded/aggregated hemoglobin (CHEBI:58751); HBA1 (HGNC:4833) —DISRUPTS→ Misfolded/aggregated hemoglobin (CHEBI:58751); Misfolded/aggregated hemoglobin (CHEBI:58751) —DISRUPTS→ Cellular protein quality control and degradation (GO:0006457); Cellular protein quality control and degradation (GO:0006457) —LEADS_TO→ Heinz body anemia (HP:0001876). Loss-of-function mutations in MANBA impair lysosomal hydrolysis in beta-mannosidosis, leading to oligosaccharidosis. Concurrently, mutations in HBA2 or HBA1 can lead to the production of unstable hemoglobin, resulting in misfolded and aggregated hemoglobin. The cellular machinery responsible for protein quality control and degradation (pathway n7) is a convergence point, as it must deal with both the accumulation of undegraded oligosaccharides (indirectly affecting protein homeostasis) and the direct burden of misfolded hemoglobin aggregates in Heinz body anemia. Dysregulation of this shared protein degradation pathway contributes to the pathogenesis of both conditions.
